attempted_axis: Execute the run-45 AF record's mandatory hypothesis -- un-static atree_handles/atree_scroll/whichatree/natreelists, close fn_8001267C source-exact at the resulting GLOBAL-linkage codegen, delete its webfrank rule and flip the TU -- and verify the premise that the global storage class is the only thing between atree and a flip.

attributes.decisive_finding: TWO INDEPENDENT BLOCKERS, NEITHER OF WHICH THE AF RECORD MEASURED, AND THE FIRST ONE KILLS ITS PLAN OUTRIGHT. (1) BSS ORDER. Our MWCC lays out EXTERNAL-linkage .bss objects in the order of their FIRST EMITTED USE, not declaration order (probes A/B: two opposite declaration orders give one identical layout; probe G: changing which array the first .bss-using function touches moves that array to offset 0; probes E/F: references that never reach codegen do not count). Static objects keep declaration order in one anonymous ...bss.0 block, and that block is emitted BEFORE any global (probe C). Retail's layout is atree_handles@0, atree_scroll@0x60, whichatree@0x1E0 -- pure declaration order -- while retail's FIRST .bss user, AtreeInitLists at 0x80010DF4, materialises `whichatree` (bss+0x1E0) directly. A first-use-ordered layout cannot put its first-used object at 0x1E0, so the retail object's .bss was NOT laid out by our rule, and no arrangement of `static` and non-static across these three arrays reproduces it while still exporting the names pb_diag.o needs. The AF hypothesis 'un-static them, close fn_8001267C at that codegen, delete its rule, flip' therefore cannot flip the TU even if fn_8001267C closed exact: atree_handles would sit at 0x8023D000 instead of 0x8023CFA0 and every pb_diag relocation into that block would resolve to the wrong address. (2) TEXT ORDER, and this one is invisible to every score in the project. atree.c's 36 functions all read real 0 or MATCH, yet our object emits TWO GROUPS in the wrong order: ours is AtreeFindNodeIdx@0x16c, AtreeFindNode@0x20c against the target's AtreeFindNode@0x16c, AtreeFindNodeIdx@0x228; and ours is AtreeSetEmpty@0x3a8, AtreeAlloc@0x424, AtreeInitLists@0x514, AtreeListLock@0x5a4 against the target's AtreeInitLists@0x3a8, AtreeListLock@0x438, AtreeAlloc@0x464, AtreeSetEmpty@0x554. Both groups re-synchronise (at 0x2c8 and 0x5d0), so the sizes are right and only the ORDER is wrong -- which is exactly why nothing caught it: fndiff pairs functions BY NAME and never compares position. The two mis-ordered functions are precisely the two that get INLINED (target AtreeFindNode 47 insns contains AtreeFindNodeIdx's strncmp loop; target AtreeAlloc 60 insns contains AtreeSetEmpty's two clearing loops), and the target emits each inlinee immediately AFTER its inliner. Our MWCC emits strictly in source order and requires the inlinee to be defined BEFORE the inliner to inline it at all, so the two constraints are in direct conflict: probes H and I put the definitions in the target's order and lost both inlines (real 0 -> 54 and real 0 -> 31). Probe J rules out `static` as the trigger for the deferral. atree is therefore substantially further from a flip than 'one function and one pin'.
attributes.law_screen: claim.law.bss-reverse-declaration-order.20260829.v1 SCREENED and MEASURED WRONG FOR THIS CASE: it describes COMMON allocation under -common on, and these objects are real `g O .bss` definitions in the object, not COMMON; their order is decided inside MWCC, and reversing the declaration list changed NOTHING (see probes A/B). claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges.20260831.v1 SCREENED: consistent with what was measured -- the static and global spellings of the SAME array produce different addressing webs -- but it says nothing about section layout, which is the actual blocker. claim.law.symbolified-own-pool-literal-blocks-tu-flip.20260831.v1 carried forward from the AF record for the .sdata2 half; untouched by this pass and still open. claim.law.identical-multiset-is-blind-to-displacements.20260831.v1 APPLIED to read the fn_8001267C delta correctly (the stw/stwx and 96-vs-192 displacement rows are the SAME fold, not four residuals).
attributes.probed_form: SEVEN probes, all reverted. A: all four objects un-statered in declaration order `s32 atree_handles[24]; u8 atree_scroll[24][16]; void* whichatree[24];` -> object .bss becomes whichatree@0, atree_handles@0x60, atree_scroll@0xC0; fn_8001267C real 72 -> 82. B: the SAME three declared in REVERSED order `void* whichatree[24]; u8 atree_scroll[24][16]; s32 atree_handles[24];` -> BYTE-IDENTICAL .bss layout to A, proving declaration order is not the key. C: only atree_handles global, atree_scroll and whichatree left static -> .bss becomes atree_scroll@0, whichatree@0x180, atree_handles@0x1E0, i.e. the static anonymous block FIRST in declaration order and the global appended AFTER; fn_8001267C real 87 and count parity lost (575/574). D: all three global with `= { 0 }` initialisers -> they leave .bss entirely and land in .data, which grows 0x60 -> 0x2A0 and destroys the TU's byte-exact .data claim. E: all three global plus a static helper `static s32 MF_probe_helper(s32 i) { return atree_handles[i] + atree_scroll[i][0] + (s32)whichatree[i]; }` placed above every other function -> the helper IS emitted (at .text +0x0, so MWCC does not dead-strip an uncalled static) and the .bss order did NOT move. F: the same three references inside a dead `if (0) { ... }` block at the top of DoTexMods -> eliminated before .bss allocation, .text size unchanged at 0x2d70, layout unchanged. G: the FIRST emitted .bss use changed from whichatree to atree_handles by rewriting AtreeInitLists's clear loop as `atree_handles[i] = 0;` -> layout became atree_handles@0, whichatree@0x60, atree_scroll@0xC0, i.e. it FOLLOWED the change. Plus two function-order probes: H, swapping the definitions of AtreeFindNodeIdx and AtreeFindNode (with a forward declaration added) -> AtreeFindNode 47/47 real 0 becomes 47/23 real 54, because AtreeFindNodeIdx is no longer defined before its caller and stops being inlined; I, reordering AtreeSetEmpty/AtreeAlloc/AtreeInitLists/AtreeListLock into the target's address order -> AtreeAlloc 60/60 real 0 becomes 60/31 real 31 for the same reason. J: `static void AtreeSetEmpty(void)` with the original order -> emission order unchanged, so the deferral is not a static-vs-global effect.
attributes.residual: atree remains Object(NonMatching). Its .text and per-function scores are as good as the AF record said (36/36 real 0 or rule-served), but the flip needs, in order: (a) a mechanism that emits an inlined helper's out-of-line copy after its inliner, which is a COMPILER-VARIANT question and belongs to the sanctioned compiler-variant hunt, not to a source lane; (b) a .bss layout mechanism that is declaration-ordered under external linkage, which is very likely the same variant question; and only then (c) fn_8001267C's remaining real 72 (two live-zero copy-form sites at +0x1e0 and +0x378, currently served by its webfrank rule) and (d) the .sdata2 orphan double at 0x80345840 that AF left unclaimed.

denial.falsifier: A compiler flag, pragma or MWCC variant in build/compilers that makes external-linkage .bss objects lay out in declaration order, or that emits an inlined helper's out-of-line copy after its inliner. Either one reopens the whole plan; the second also fixes the .text order without losing the inlines.
denial.premise_measurement: With all three arrays non-static the object's .bss is whichatree@0x0, atree_handles@0x60, atree_scroll@0xC0 (objdump -t on build/GUNE5D/src/game/anim/.postprocess/body/atree.o), against retail's atree_handles@0x8023CFA0, atree_scroll@0x8023D000, whichatree@0x8023D180 in config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt. Declaration order does not change it (probes A and B are byte-identical), and the layout follows first EMITTED use (probe G moved atree_handles to offset 0 by making AtreeInitLists touch it first). Separately, our .text emits AtreeFindNodeIdx before AtreeFindNode and AtreeSetEmpty/AtreeAlloc before AtreeInitLists/AtreeListLock, where retail emits the reverse in both groups.
denial.scope: The specific run-45 plan for game/anim/atree: 'give the four .bss/.sbss objects external linkage, close fn_8001267C source-exact at that codegen, delete its webfrank rule, and flip'. It denies nothing about fn_8001267C's closability, about the TU's data claims, or about a flip achieved by some other mechanism.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Compile atree.c unchanged with each archived MWCC and run `objdump -t` on the result: if no variant produces AtreeFindNode before AtreeFindNodeIdx while AtreeFindNode is still 47 instructions, the deferral is not a compiler-version fact and the .text order must come from a source structure we have not reconstructed (for example a dead-stripped static helper, which the AF record already suspected from the orphan .sdata2 double at 0x80345840).

AtreeFindNode` (47 instructions containing AtreeFindNodeIdx's strncmp loop and its ErrorPrintf).
hypothesis.statement: Both blockers are one fact about the compiler, not two about the source: retail's atree.o was built by an MWCC configuration that (i) assigns .bss offsets at DECLARATION time rather than at first use and (ii) defers an inlined function's out-of-line body until after its inliners. Run the sanctioned compiler-variant sweep over build/compilers against atree.c with the three arrays non-static, and score the variant on the two ORDER facts (objdump -t .bss order; objdump -t .text order) rather than on any fndiff percentage, because both facts are invisible to every score the project currently computes.
